translation_notes: prefixes: RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, OWL->owl, SKOS->skos, DCTERMS->dcterms, XSD->xsd, PROV->prov (the `from rdflib.namespace import ...` line is a context line of the file, kept verbatim: other regions of build_page_v6_9_0.py use those constants, and removing it would be cleaning)

the four `g.remove((iri, P, None))` are the textbook case of the stratum: an unbound variable in `-{ }` is the joker, so `g.remove((iri, RDFS.label, None))` becomes `-{ {iri} rdfs:label ?o }`. The stand-in ABox gives semtech:Protege TWO rdfs:label values, so a removal that did not wildcard leaves a stale triple: replacing `?o` by the literal makes the driver report 17 vs 18 triples (mutation checked)

LIMIT FOUND (new): `+{ }` / `-{ }` are recognised only at the start of a LOGICAL line, and the region writes each pair on the suite of a one-line `if`: `if label is not None: g.remove(...); g.add(...)`. After a `;` both islands are recognised (verified), but after `if ...: ` they are NOT -- the transpiler leaves `-{ {iri} rdfs:label ?o }` untouched and the emitted file fails to compile (`SyntaxError: invalid syntax` on the half-transpiled prefixed name). The failure is loud, not silent, but the translation has to break each one-line `if` into a three-line block. Hence minor-restructuring: same statements, same order, only the layout changes. Extending the capture to the first token of a compound-statement suite would remove the last restructuring in this region
the module-level `@graph g` is declared once and reaches inside redefine() (block scope), which is what lets the four rewritten pairs drop the `g.` receiver entirely
`Literal(label, lang="en")` -> `{label}@en` (interpolation with a glued language tag), not `"label"@en`: the value is computed

context shim (identical for both sides, excluded from the surface metrics): the preamble parses `f"{HERE}/04-page/semtech_page_abox_v6_8_0.ttl"`, and neither HERE nor that ABox is in the extract. context_shim.py binds HERE to the example directory and 04-page/semtech_page_abox_v6_8_0.ttl is a minimal stand-in (two labels on one subject, a subject without skos:definition, and neighbouring predicates/subjects that must survive). context_shim.replay() holds the calls the module makes to redefine() further down the file -- also outside the region -- so the mutation of the module-level `g` is observable by the isomorphism oracle; the pair itself gains one identical line, `replay(redefine)`
oracle: entry=None (module state). redefine() returns None and takes no graph argument, so an entry=... driver would compare nothing; the graph it mutates is a module global

Audit du 2026-10-31 (traduction juste) : les quatre gardes `is not None` n'étaient exercées qu'avec None ou des chaînes non vides, si bien qu'une garde affaiblie en `if label:` restait verte ; le pilote rejoue maintenant, après le replay du shim, les trois appels réels du dépôt (sp:Page, sp:ReferencesRegion, sp:Doc, build_page_v6_9_0.py:66-73) puis des chaînes vides (note="", scope="", label="", defn=""), qui retirent l'ancienne valeur et écrivent un littéral vide @en : les quatre affaiblissements tombent, la traduction passe. Le fixture porte l'en-tête @prefix réel (les sujets du shim, dans un espace inventé que le vrai en-tête lie à un autre semtech:, sont écrits en IRI complètes) et le pilote compare les liaisons de g, que le dépôt sérialise (ligne 106) : les sept @prefix de la traduction portent les noms que le fichier lie déjà, un @prefix sk: ou rs: écraserait. Les deux versions, exécutées contre le vrai semtech_page_abox_v6_8_0.ttl du dépôt, sont équivalentes. 'interpolation {expr}' ({iri}, {label}@en…) ajouté aux constructions, où il manquait.
